Something else we'll probably want to do in follow-up are explicit `ref pin mut` / `ref pin const` binding modes.

E.g., we can write today:

```rust
fn f<T>(&mut [ref mut x]: &mut [T; 1]) -> &mut T { x }
```

Probably we'd similarly want something along the lines of:

```rust
fn f<T>(&pin mut [ref pin mut x]: &pin mut [T; 1]) -> &pin mut T { x }
```

> This is because errors should be sorted in ascending order, prioritizing the rightmost occurrence.

Why do we need to report rightmost occurrence first?

For code:
```rust
fn check_format_args() {
    print!("{:?} {:?} {a} {a:?}", [], [], a = 1 + 1);
}
```

Without `Reverse` the error report is:

```console
error[E0282]: type annotations needed
 --> tests/ui/errors/span-format_args-issue-140578.rs:2:35
  |
2 |     print!("{:?} {:?} {a} {a:?}", [], [], a = 1 + 1);
  |                                   ^^ cannot infer type
  |
```

With `Reverse` the error report is:
```console
error[E0282]: type annotations needed
 --> tests/ui/errors/span-format_args-issue-140578.rs:2:39
  |
2 |     print!("{:?} {:?} {a} {a:?}", [], [], a = 1 + 1);
  |                                       ^^ cannot infer type
  |
```

I think it's more natural to report the leftmost occurrence?
